### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **43** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (42 routes)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cd3b4682fb954c3ae169305e4aa8a0a8a8aaa900` — the merge of head `7bef635bb2e5405aee033ef40cf9154af1de4785` into base `cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cd3b4682fb954c3ae169305e4aa8a0a8a8aaa900 && git checkout cd3b4682fb954c3ae169305e4aa8a0a8a8aaa900
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b 7bef635bb2e5405aee033ef40cf9154af1de4785 && git checkout -B drift-repro cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b && git merge --no-ff 7bef635bb2e5405aee033ef40cf9154af1de4785

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `7bef635bb2e5405aee033ef40cf9154af1de4785`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: a new `sys_audit_log` action value and row, an additive declared output (`Clause-②: yes` on the claim 6712396285, PR body and changeset). No path under `packages/spec/**`, no governed path, no new error code, no route. Diff read in full: 28 files, +850/−42 (11 of them the generated translations of the one new label).
- **Seat ruling followed (A).** One call, in the verb `deletePackage` (metadata-protocol) after the cleanups and before the return — the one place every door that reaches the verb passes. The version is read beside `captureUninstallDeclared`, before the registry withdrawal; nothing near `assertPackageUninstallable` moves, which keeps #31232's guard hunk apart.
- **The plugin owns the row shape; the verb hands an event.** `recordPackageLifecycleEvent` sits on the `audit` slot beside the auth, action-invocation and export writers (the #27908 pattern); metadata-protocol declares the event structurally and does not depend on plugin-audit. No audit slot ⇒ no row, no throw; a writer that throws anyway is logged, never answered (the uninstall already completed).
- **When a row is written.** Only after a successful verb run, and only when there was a package (registry held it, or the store bound items to it): a refusal throws earlier, and an id that was never a package (the door's 404) writes none. A partial uninstall writes `outcome: 'partial'` with its counts.
- **Row.** `action: 'package_uninstall'`; `actor` two-valued, `user_id` only for a human principal (`svc:` stays in `actor`), as the CRUD mirror writes it; no `object_name` / `record_id`; `tenant_id` null ⇒ a deployment-level row, readable by platform admins only (declared). `metadata`: package id, version, environment, keep_data, items removed / failed, outcome. The lost-row path is a named durability callee (`persistPackageLifecycleAuditRow`) registered in both durability gate vocabularies, reported once per cause at `error`.

### ② Semver level

- Additive: a new enum option and a new row on a path that answered the same before. No caller's answer changes. Changesets `@objectstack/plugin-audit` + `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security / read visibility: the row names no organization, so tenant-scoped readers never see it; platform admins read it through the existing unfiltered views. The row records no params beyond the package's own identity.
- Declared surface beyond the claim, accepted: the two durability gate vocabularies (one line each, as #31000), the tenant-audit census docs (one more write site), and a two-line `environmentId` getter on the protocol host.
- Not closed here, filed: install-local's own `DELETE /marketplace/install-local/:id` bypasses the verb, so it writes no row → #31283 (with #31232's guard gap on the same door).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-abxjas`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2dLQEXWGsE2SZ3Qn5F`

**VERDICT: PASS**

The reviewed diff is unchanged: same `git patch-id --stable` against the merge base at `70ebe57f` and at `7bef635b`. Audit 6714952345 covers the two flake runs.
